questions.recWhy: Pages CMS edits markdown in a repository, is MIT with 3,976 stars, has no paid tier, and lists inline comments as Soon, so the review-shaped hole is visible and named by the incumbent itself. Developers deploy from repositories at scale, 443,392 root CNAME files and 113,536 Astro configs, and these people already keep documents in git, so the review file needs no explaining to them. What the two-week test needs most is named people, and G15's cold list has to come from somewhere; this audience is a pool that costs no permission, no build and no channel hours. What it is not is a paying channel. No paid tier anywhere in view means they are trained to expect this free, and Q13 already gives the editor away, so the pool feeds the stranger test rather than the price test. If a Pages CMS user in the pilot says they would pay, the audience becomes a channel and gets its own page.
